title: Four o'clock at the bakery
summary: A teenager starts a summer job at a bakery and discovers what happens while the town sleeps.
paragraphs: Nobody had told Inés that bakers start work in the middle of the night. When Mr Castro offered her a summer job, she imagined selling cakes to friendly customers in the afternoon. Then he said, "See you on Monday. Four o'clock. In the morning."

On the first day her alarm went off at half past three, and she almost went back to sleep. The streets were empty and silent. Only the bakery had a light on, and the smell of warm bread came out of the door like an {{invitation}}.

Mr Castro gave her an {{apron}} and showed her how to measure flour and water. "Bread is simple," he said. "Flour, water, salt, yeast and time. The difficult part is the time." The dough had to rest, then be shaped, then rest again. While they waited, he made coffee and told her stories about the town.

At six o'clock the first customers arrived: a bus driver, two nurses finishing a night {{shift}}, a man who walked his dog at the same hour every day. They all knew Mr Castro, and soon they knew Inés too. She learnt that the nurses liked the bread a little burnt and that the bus driver always bought one extra roll for a colleague.

By the end of July, Inés could shape twenty loaves in ten minutes. She was tired, but she was also proud. On her last day, Mr Castro gave her a small paper bag. Inside there was a jar of his {{sourdough}} starter, the living mixture that makes his bread rise. "Look after it," he said. "Feed it every day, and it will last longer than both of us."

invitation.meaning: a request to come somewhere, here something that makes you want to go in

apron.meaning: a piece of cloth you wear over your clothes to keep them clean when cooking

shift.meaning: a period of work, for example at night

sourdough.meaning: bread made with a mixture of flour and water that is kept alive for a long time

questions.question: What did Inés think the job would be like?
options: Working all night in a factory
Cleaning the bakery after it closed
questions.explanation: She imagined selling cakes to friendly customers in the afternoon.

questions.question: According to Mr Castro, what is the difficult part of making bread?
questions.explanation: He said bread is simple and that the difficult part is the time.

questions.question: Who were some of the first customers?
options: Students on their way to school
A bus driver and two nurses
questions.explanation: At six o'clock a bus driver, two nurses and a man with a dog arrived.

questions.question: What was the present Mr Castro gave Inés?
options: A cake with her name on it
A jar of his sourdough starter
questions.explanation: Inside the paper bag there was a jar of his sourdough starter.
